rationale: Assign first: household has low liquid buffer (LIQ + CDS + NMMF below max($5k, 2 months normal income)) or credit-constraint/revolving-debt indicator, and net interest-sensitive position is <=0. Includes poor hand-to-mouth and debt-exposed wealthy hand-to-mouth.

Residual working-age/non-retired household with housing/retirement illiquid assets or mortgage/HELOC exposure after constrained, retiree saver, and unconstrained saver assignment. Captures middle balance sheets where mortgage cash-flow channel matters.

Age >=65 or retired, wage income share low, positive interest-sensitive assets (LIQ/CDS/NMMF/BOND/direct Treasury) or material INTDIVINC, and not liquidity-constrained. Separate because interest-income MPC and asset mix differ from working-age savers.
Top-wealth/high-financial-asset household with liquid buffer >=6 months normal income and positive net interest exposure; not fixed-income retiree. Low near-term conversion but large asset holdings.
Noncorporate/private or small employer, no bond-market access, majority of interest-bearing debt from banks/floating C&I/credit lines. Higher cash-flow to investment/working-capital response.
Corporate/large/public or bond/syndicated-loan borrower with market access and liquid buffers. Lower cash-flow conversion; rate-side cost-of-capital overlay remains separate.
